* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Cheyenne County in northwestern Kansas...
Rawlins County in northwestern Kansas...
Hitchcock County in southwestern Nebraska...
Dundy County in southwestern Nebraska...

* Until 1215 AM MDT/115 AM CDT/.

* At 1057 PM MDT/1157 PM CDT/, severe thunderstorms were located
along a line extending from 10 miles northwest of Stratton to 7
miles southeast of Haigler, moving southeast at 40 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

building.

flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Dust Storm Warning issued August 9 at 10:23PM MST until August 9 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
At 1020 PM MST, a wall of dust was along a line extending from near
Aguila to 17 miles northwest of Tonopah to 8 miles southwest of Palo
Verde Nuclear Generation Station, moving west at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Less than one quarter mile with strong wind in excess of
50 mph.

SOURCE...Doppler radar.

IMPACT...Dangerous life-threatening travel.

This includes the following highways...
AZ Interstate 10 between mile markers 64 and 95.
US Highway 60 between mile markers 66 and 95.

Locations impacted include...
Tonopah, Gladden, and Aguila.
properties.instruction:
Dust storms lead to dangerous driving conditions with visibility
reduced to near zero. If driving, avoid dust storms if possible. If
caught in one, then pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep
your foot off the brake.

Motorists should not drive into a dust storm. PULL ASIDE STAY ALIVE!

Strong to severe thunderstorms are also possible behind this wall of
dust. Keep updated with this quickly evolving situation.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 9 at 9:46PM CDT until August 10 at 12:45AM CDT by NWS Huntsville AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Madison County in north central Alabama...

* WHEN...Until 1245 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 942 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges measured 2
to 3" of rainfall in about half an hour earlier this evening,
with rainfall totals between 3-4" estimated in portions of
Northern and Western Huntsville. Local creeks in the city rose
several feet in an hour as a result. Indian Creek at Madison also
rose 4 feet during this time, and it continues to slowly rise.
Indian Creek should crest between 7 and 8 feet around or after
midnight, and slowly fall through sunrise.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Huntsville, Madison, Redstone Arsenal, Triana, Marshall Space
Flight Center, University Of Alabama In Huntsville, Huntsville
International Airport and Alabama A And M University.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
